description: Kessler is an open-source Python package for simulation-based inference and machine learning for spacecraft collision avoidance and assessment, named after NASA scientist Donald J. Kessler. It imports and exports conjunction data messages, provides Bayesian and explainable machine learning models for conjunction risk, and includes a novel generative model of conjunction data messages. It covers low Earth orbit conjunction analysis in general, not one mission. It was initiated by the Constellations team at the Frontier Development Lab Europe 2020, a partnership of ESA, Trillium Technologies and the University of Oxford, together with the European Space Operations Centre, with Giacomo Acciarini as main developer; it was presented at the 8th European Conference on Space Debris in 2021 and version 1.0.1 was released on PyPI on 24 April 2025, also on conda-forge. It is free under GPL-3.0, with other licensing options on request. Caveats: models need training data such as real conjunction messages, and outputs are research-grade, not certified operational products. It supports hazard exposure, resilience and emergency response planning for satellites facing debris; a related record is the ESA Collision Avoidance Challenge dataset.
